title: Glycerol and Glucose Assays by GC-mass Spectrometry
author: Henri Brunengraber
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ydkfs4w

steps.title: Add sample and IS
steps.instruction: Place 20 µL plasma or 50 mg tissue into a glass screw‑top tube and add ~20 µL of [2H5]glycerol internal standard for concentration measurement.

steps.title: Hydrolyze total glycerol
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of 1 M KOH in 70 % ethanol (KOH‑EtOH) to the tube, then heat at 80 °C for 3 h on a heating block to hydrolyze glyceride esters.

steps.title: Acidify hydrolysate
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of 6 N HCl to the heated mixture.

steps.title: Extract with chloroform
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL chloroform, vortex for 2 min, transfer the mixture to an Eppendorf tube and centrifuge for 2 min.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Remove the top aqueous layer, place it in a clean test tube and evaporate to dryness under a stream of nitrogen gas.

steps.title: Derivatize glycerol
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL pyridine and 50 µL acetic anhydride (1:1 v/v, total 100 µL) to the dried residue, then heat on a heating block until the solvent is completely removed (do not over‑dry).

steps.title: Add running solvent
steps.instruction: Add 70 µL ethyl acetate; this serves as the GC‑MS injection solvent.

steps.title: GC‑MS analysis glycerol
steps.instruction: Transfer the 70 µL solution to a GC autosampler insert and run GC‑MS using an Agilent 5973N‑MSD coupled to an Agilent 6890 GC with a DB‑17MS column (30 m × 0.25 mm × 0.25 µm) under ammonia chemical ionization; monitor SIM m/z 236, 237, 238 for glycerol‑triacetate.

steps.title: Free glycerol extraction
steps.instruction: For free glycerol, after adding sample and IS, skip the KOH‑EtOH addition, heating, and HCl step; directly add 300 µL chloroform, vortex 2 min, transfer, centrifuge 2 min, then continue with steps 5‑8 as described for total glycerol.

steps.title: Add glucose sample and IS
steps.instruction: Place 10 µL blood sample into an Eppendorf tube and add 10 µL of 1 mg mL⁻¹ uniformly 13C‑ or 2H‑labeled glucose internal standard (ribose may be used for 13C glucose labeling assays).

steps.title: Precipitate proteins with methanol
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL methanol to the tube, vortex briefly, and centrifuge for ~2 min.

steps.title: Collect supernatant and dry
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a clean test tube and evaporate to dryness under nitrogen gas.

steps.title: Derivatize glucose
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL pyridine and 50 µL acetic anhydride (1:1 v/v, total 100 µL) to the dried residue, then heat on a heating block at 80 °C until completely dry (do not over‑dry).

steps.title: Add running solvent
steps.instruction: Add 70 µL ethyl acetate as the GC‑MS injection solvent.

steps.title: GC‑MS analysis glucose
steps.instruction: Transfer the solution to a GC autosampler insert and run GC‑MS under the same instrument conditions as glycerol; monitor SIM m/z 408–414 for glucose‑pentaacetate (M0–M6).
